claim_summary: TimeRSI uses forecasting feedback to revise deployment pipelines around frozen time-series foundation models, then selects a pipeline for each new forecast using similar completed windows.

claim_evidence.quote: A coding agent translates task descriptions into executable pipeline changes.
uses observed errors to guide subsequent revisions.

modules.name: Iterative forecasting pipeline improvement
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the revision loop scores candidate forecasting pipelines by forecast error and changes the forecasting procedure; if the task family changed, its forecast output, objective, and validation windows would need redesign. R3_2_GTS would fit only if it handled temporal windows without a task-specific forecast objective; R3_3_GH would fit only if it managed generic execution without temporal or forecast semantics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - pipeline revisions optimize forecasting output using forecast errors
R3_2_GTS:no - temporal windows are evaluated against a forecasting objective
R3_3_GH:no - the loop has temporal forecasting semantics

evidence.quote: The loop starts from direct TSFM inference as the reference pipeline. In each iteration, the agent uses the task description and earlier results to propose and implement a code revision. The system executes it on the adaptation windows and returns forecasting scores, window-level errors, and execution logs.
The agent writes Python code across four stages: preprocessing, feature construction, context selection, and post-processing.

modules.name: Similarity-weighted historical pipeline selection
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the selector ranks forecasting pipelines by their forecast errors under similar conditions; changing task family would require a different output objective and loss. R3_2_GTS would fit temporal retrieval independent of one task objective, while R3_3_GH would fit generic selection with no temporal or task-specific forecast semantics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - candidate choice minimizes forecasting error
R3_2_GTS:no - retrieval is explicitly conditioned on forecasting error
R3_3_GH:no - similarity and completed-window state have temporal semantics

evidence.quote: A pipeline that performs well on average may not be the best choice for every future window. T IME RSI therefore selects a pipeline for each target variable at each new forecast origin.
At a new origin, the selector first filters out windows whose outcomes are not yet complete.

temporal_validity.quote: The evaluator supplies the same chronological windows to all candidates. Candidate code receives no target values beyond each window’s origin.

task_performance.quote: T IME RSI achieves the best scores among all existing submissions across six point and probabilistic forecasting metrics.

notes: The paper reports execution logs and traces, but its experiments do not separately score execution success or failure handling as process-validity evidence.
